Riyadh-Saudi Arabia.name: Riyadh
Riyadh-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Lorimer (1908) and Philby estimate c. 14k-18k following Ibn Saud's 1902 recapture, rising with royal capital consolidation to 83k by 1950, 169,185 in the 1962/63 Saudi municipal census, and ~420k by 1971 on trajectory to 666,840 in the 1974 census.

Jeddah-Saudi Arabia.name: Jeddah
Jeddah-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Late Ottoman Hejaz salnames and consular reports give ~28k-30k before WWI disruption and the 1924-25 siege; rapid post-1947 wall demolition and oil-era port expansion reached 147,859 in 1962/63 and ~380k in 1971 (561,104 in 1974 census).

Mecca-Saudi Arabia.name: Mecca
Mecca-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Ottoman Hejaz administrative estimates and Arab Bureau Handbook of Arabia (1916) record ~70k-75k permanent residents, expanding to 158,908 in the 1962/63 census and ~310k in 1971 (366,801 in the 1974 Saudi census).

Kuwait City-Kuwait.name: Kuwait City
Kuwait City-Kuwait.evidence_basis: Lorimer (1908) estimates ~35k in walled Kuwait Town; post-1946 oil boom and Kuwait official censuses record 104,551 (1957), 151,000 (1965), and 217,749 (1970 Capital urban core).

Medina-Saudi Arabia.name: Medina
Medina-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Hejaz Railway terminus (1908) lifted Medina to ~40k before Ottoman evacuation during the 1916-19 siege cut residents to ~15k; steady Saudi-era recovery reached 72,000 in 1962/63 and ~160k by 1971 (198,186 in 1974 census).

Taif-Saudi Arabia.name: Taif
Taif-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Ottoman summer resort and garrison of ~8k-9.5k (Handbook of Arabia 1916), expanding rapidly as Saudi summer seat and military hub to 54,000 in 1962/63 and ~150k by 1971 (204,857-211,095 in 1974 census).

Sanaa-Yemen.name: Sanaa
Sanaa-Yemen.evidence_basis: Ottoman vilayet seat (~35k in 1900) severely depopulated by the 1904-05 siege and famine (~25k), recovering under Imam Yahya (~45k in 1930) and accelerating after the 1962 YAR revolution to ~115k in 1971 (134,588 in 1975 YAR census).

Hawalli-Kuwait.name: Hawalli
Hawalli-Kuwait.evidence_basis: Founded in 1906 as a sweet-water well village outside Kuwait City, exploding during 1950s-60s Arab expatriate immigration to 106,542 in the 1970 Kuwait census.

Al-Hofuf-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Hofuf
Al-Hofuf-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Lorimer (1908) estimates 25,000 souls in the walled capital of Al-Hasa oasis (Ottoman until 1913); steady Saudi growth reached ~83k in 1962/63 and ~98k in 1971 (101,271 in 1974 census).

Dammam-Saudi Arabia.name: Dammam
Dammam-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Re-founded in 1923 by Al-Dawasir migrants from Bahrain (~1.5k-2k); transformed after 1938 oil discovery, 1951 Dammam-Riyadh railway, and provincial capital transfer (1953) to ~32k in 1962 and ~95k in 1971 (127,844 in 1974 census).

Manama-Bahrain.name: Manama
Manama-Bahrain.evidence_basis: Lorimer (1908) estimates 25,000 souls, followed by exact Bahrain official censuses: 27,835 (1941), 39,648 (1950), 61,726 (1959), 79,098 (1965), and 88,785 (1971).

Dubai-United Arab Emirates.name: Dubai
Dubai-United Arab Emirates.evidence_basis: Lorimer (1908) estimates 10,000 souls (~335 pearling boats); merchant migration from Lingeh and creek-dredging entrepot boom lifted it to 58,971 in the 1968 Trucial States census and ~85k by 1971.

Doha-Qatar.name: Doha
Doha-Qatar.evidence_basis: Lorimer (1908) estimates 12,000 souls (incl. 350 Ottoman troops); contracted during the 1930s pearl crash before post-1949 oil exports drove it to 80,000 in Qatar's 1970 census.

Taiz-Yemen.name: Taiz
Taiz-Yemen.evidence_basis: Southern highland provincial town (~10k in 1900) that expanded sharply when Imam Ahmad made it the Mutawakkilite royal capital (1948-62), reaching ~65k by 1971 (78,642 in 1975 YAR census).

Salmiya-Kuwait.name: Salmiya
Salmiya-Kuwait.evidence_basis: Planned urban development inaugurated around 1950 on the Ras al-Ard promontory (replacing fishing village Dimnah), surging to 67,346 in the 1970 Kuwait census.

Al-Hudaydah-Yemen.name: Al-Hudaydah
Al-Hudaydah-Yemen.evidence_basis: Primary Ottoman Yemeni Red Sea port (~40k in 1900 per Arab Bureau 1916; NID 1946 notes interwar decline to ~35k), expanding after 1961 modern port opening to ~70k in 1971 (80,314 in 1975 YAR census).

Buraydah-Saudi Arabia.name: Buraydah
Buraydah-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Lorimer (1908) and Philby place Qasim's administrative capital at ~10k, growing as central Najd commercial hub to ~35k in 1962 and ~58k in 1971 (69,940 in 1974 Saudi census).

Tabuk-Saudi Arabia.name: Tabuk
Tabuk-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Small oasis and 1906 Hejaz Railway station (~1.5k-2.6k in Musil and NID 1946) transformed in the 1960s by major Saudi northern military base expansion to ~52k by 1971 (74,825 in 1974 census).

Abu Dhabi-United Arab Emirates.name: Abu Dhabi
Abu Dhabi-United Arab Emirates.evidence_basis: Pearling island town (~6k in Lorimer 1908) that shrank to ~4k after the 1930s pearl collapse before 1962 oil exports and Sheikh Zayed's 1966 accession lifted it to 22,023 (1968 census) and ~46k by 1971.

Al-Mubarraz-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Mubarraz
Al-Mubarraz-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Second town of Al-Hasa oasis estimated by Lorimer (1908) at 8,500 souls, expanding with Eastern Province oil-era employment to ~45k in 1971 (54,325 in 1974 census).

Muscat-Oman.name: Muscat
Muscat-Oman.evidence_basis: Lorimer (1908) estimates 24,000 for the twin ports of Muscat (~10k) and Muttrah (~14k); interwar maritime slump eased to ~21k before post-1967 oil exports and 1970 Qaboos modernization lifted it to ~45k in 1971.

Al-Khobar-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Khobar
Al-Khobar-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Planned in 1942 as Aramco's commercial port and merchant town opposite Bahrain, booming to ~18k in 1962/63 and ~42k in 1971 (48,817 in 1974 Saudi census).

Najran-Saudi Arabia.name: Najran
Najran-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Wadi Najran oasis cluster documented by Philby (1936/1952) after 1934 Saudi incorporation, growing from ~5.5k in 1900 to ~24k in 1962 and ~41k by 1971 (47,501 in 1974 Saudi census).

Al-Mukalla-Yemen.name: Al-Mukalla
Al-Mukalla-Yemen.evidence_basis: Qu'aiti Sultanate capital and Hadramawt entrepot estimated at ~12k in 1910 and ~18k-24k by Ingrams/NID (1935-50), rising to ~41k by 1971 ahead of the 1973 PDRY census.

Al-Farwaniya-Kuwait.name: Al-Farwaniya
Al-Farwaniya-Kuwait.evidence_basis: Small interior village south of Kuwait City that urbanized rapidly during the 1960s suburban expansion, reaching ~37.6k in the 1970 Kuwait census.

Khamis Mushait-Saudi Arabia.name: Khamis Mushait
Khamis Mushait-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Shahran highland market town (~3.2k-4.5k per Philby 1936/1952) that expanded sharply in the 1960s with King Khalid Military City and airbase to ~39k by 1971 (49,581 in 1974 census).

Muharraq-Bahrain.name: Muharraq
Muharraq-Bahrain.evidence_basis: Historic Al Khalifa capital estimated at 20,000 in Lorimer (1908), then tracked across Bahrain official censuses: 21,439 (1941), 25,577 (1950), 32,302 (1959), 34,430 (1965), and 37,732 (1971).

Hail-Saudi Arabia.name: Hail
Hail-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Rashidi Emirate capital of Jabal Shammar (~12k in 1900 per Lorimer 1908 and Bell 1914) that dipped after 1921 Saudi conquest before recovering to ~22k in 1962 and ~35k in 1971 (40,502 in 1974 census).

Dhahran-Saudi Arabia.name: Dhahran
Dhahran-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Founded in 1938 around Dammam Well No. 7 as CASOC/Aramco headquarters and later airbase/KFUPM campus, expanding from ~2.5k to ~12k in 1950 and ~35k by 1971.

Al-Kharj-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Kharj
Al-Kharj-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Fertile Najdi agricultural basin surveyed by Philby (1918) and expanded by royal/Aramco irrigation projects in the 1940s and military-industrial facilities by 1971 (~34k).

Sharjah-United Arab Emirates.name: Sharjah
Sharjah-United Arab Emirates.evidence_basis: Largest Trucial port in Lorimer (1908) at ~15,000 souls; silted creek and pearl collapse caused interwar stagnation (~12.5k in 1940) before recovering to 20,621 in the 1968 census and ~31k in 1971.

Al-Qatif-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Qatif
Al-Qatif-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Lorimer (1908) records ~10,000 inhabitants in Qatif town and walled Qal'ah (~700 inner-citadel houses plus suburbs), growing steadily to ~30k by 1971.

Jizan-Saudi Arabia.name: Jizan
Jizan-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Red Sea port and Idrisi Emirate capital (~5k-7.5k in Arab Bureau 1916 and NID 1946) incorporated into Saudi Arabia in 1930-34, reaching ~29k in 1971 (32,812 in 1974 census).

Unayzah-Saudi Arabia.name: Unayzah
Unayzah-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Lorimer (1908) explicitly estimates 10,000-15,000 souls in three walled wards (~12k midpoint); prominent merchant oasis growing steadily to ~25k in 1962 and ~28.5k in 1971.

Abha-Saudi Arabia.name: Abha
Abha-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Ottoman Asir sanjak capital and highland market of ~4.2k-5.5k (Cornwallis/Arab Bureau 1916; Philby Arabian Highlands), growing as Saudi Asir provincial seat to ~27k by 1971 (30,150 in 1974 census).

Fahaheel-Kuwait.name: Fahaheel
Fahaheel-Kuwait.evidence_basis: Small coastal fishing village in Lorimer (1908) transformed after 1946 into the commercial port adjacent to Ahmadi and Mina al-Ahmadi oil terminal, reaching ~24.5k by 1970.

Al-Ahmadi-Kuwait.name: Al-Ahmadi
Al-Ahmadi-Kuwait.evidence_basis: Founded in 1946 by Kuwait Oil Company (KOC) near Burgan oilfield, tracked in Kuwait censuses at 12,860 (1957), 18,719 (1965), and 21,269 (1970).

Al-Jahra-Kuwait.name: Al-Jahra
Al-Jahra-Kuwait.evidence_basis: Fortified agricultural oasis west of Kuwait Bay (Lorimer 1908 ~1.2k; site of 1920 Battle of Jahra), growing with Bedouin settlement to ~18.9k in the 1970 Kuwait census.

Wadi ad-Dawasir-Saudi Arabia.name: Wadi ad-Dawasir
Wadi ad-Dawasir-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Southern Najd oasis cluster (Al-Khamasin/Dam) surveyed by Philby (1918, The Heart of Arabia) at ~5.5k-6.4k, growing with groundwater agriculture to ~19.8k by 1971.

Sakaka-Saudi Arabia.name: Sakaka
Sakaka-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Al-Jawf basin oasis surveyed by Musil (1909) and Philby (1922) before Saudi annexation in 1922, growing as northern administrative capital to ~19.5k by 1971.

Ras al-Khaimah-United Arab Emirates.name: Ras al-Khaimah
Ras al-Khaimah-United Arab Emirates.evidence_basis: Northern Qasimi maritime and agricultural centre estimated at ~5,000 in Lorimer (1908), reaching 16,650 town residents (24,387 emirate total) in the 1968 Trucial States census.

Arar-Saudi Arabia.name: Arar
Arar-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Founded in 1951 as the Badanah pumping station along the Trans-Arabian Pipeline (Tapline), rapidly attracting settled northern Bedouin to reach ~10.5k in 1962 and ~18.5k by 1971.

Dhamar-Yemen.name: Dhamar
Dhamar-Yemen.evidence_basis: Central Yemeni plateau market and scholarly town recorded in Arab Bureau (1916) and NID (1946), growing from ~8.5k in 1900 to ~18.5k in 1971 (~19.5k in 1975 YAR census).

Sur-Oman.name: Sur
Sur-Oman.evidence_basis: Major Omani dhow-building and Indian Ocean seafaring port estimated at ~12,000 in Lorimer (1908), stabilizing during interwar sail decline and rising to ~18k by 1971.

Bisha-Saudi Arabia.name: Bisha
Bisha-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Major Wadi Bisha date-oasis cluster surveyed by Philby (1936/1952), growing from ~3.8k in 1900 to ~17.5k by 1971 with agricultural sedentarization.

Ibb-Yemen.name: Ibb
Ibb-Yemen.evidence_basis: Walled highland agricultural capital of the fertile Ibb basin (NID 1946; 1975 YAR census provincial seat), growing steadily from ~7.5k in 1900 to ~17.5k by 1971.

Ar-Rass-Saudi Arabia.name: Ar-Rass
Ar-Rass-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Lorimer (1908) explicitly estimates 3,500 souls along Wadi ar-Rummah in western Qasim; steady agrarian and town expansion brought it to ~16.5k by 1971.

Ras Tanura-Saudi Arabia.name: Ras Tanura
Ras Tanura-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Established in 1939 as Saudi Arabia's first oil export terminal and 1945 refinery town (Rahimah), growing with Aramco workforce to ~16.5k by 1971.

Sayun-Yemen.name: Sayun
Sayun-Yemen.evidence_basis: Kathiri Sultanate capital in Wadi Hadramawt documented by Van der Meulen (1932) and Ingrams (1936), growing with Hadrami diaspora remittances to ~16.5k by 1971.

Hafar al-Batin-Saudi Arabia.name: Hafar al-Batin
Hafar al-Batin-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Traditional Wadi al-Batin wells and tribal market documented by Lorimer (1908) and Dickson, growing rapidly after Tapline road construction (1950s) to ~15.5k by 1971.

Dawadmi-Saudi Arabia.name: Dawadmi
Dawadmi-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Western Najd Otaibah settlement and royal highway waystation documented in Philby and Alruwais (1998), growing through post-1930s Bedouin sedentarization to ~14.8k by 1971.

Tarim-Yemen.name: Tarim
Tarim-Yemen.evidence_basis: Eastern Wadi Hadramawt religious and merchant town funded by Southeast Asian diaspora remittances (Van der Meulen 1932; Ingrams 1936), expanding from ~8k to ~14.8k by 1971.

Al-Qurayyat-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Qurayyat
Al-Qurayyat-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Wadi Sirhan salt-trading oasis (Kaf/Qurayyat) incorporated into Saudi Arabia by the 1925 Hadda Agreement, expanding as a customs and border market to ~14.5k by 1971.

Al-Zulfi-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Zulfi
Al-Zulfi-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Northern Najd oasis and caravan station on the Kuwait-Qasim track recorded in Lorimer (1908) at ~3.8k, rising with Bedouin settlement to ~14.2k by 1971.

Abqaiq-Saudi Arabia.name: Abqaiq
Abqaiq-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Founded in 1940 upon discovery of the giant Abqaiq oilfield as an Aramco camp and adjacent Arab town, growing to ~8.8k in 1962 and ~14.2k by 1971.

Lahij-Yemen.name: Lahij
Lahij-Yemen.evidence_basis: Abdali Sultanate capital in Wadi Tuban oasis supplying Aden (Arab Bureau 1916; NID 1946 estimate ~8k-10k), reaching ~14.2k by 1971 as Governorate II seat.

Sohar-Oman.name: Sohar
Sohar-Oman.evidence_basis: Lorimer (1908) explicitly estimates 7,500 souls along the Al-Batinah palm belt, growing gradually as northern coastal centre to ~14k by 1971.

Al-Wakrah-Qatar.name: Al-Wakrah
Al-Wakrah-Qatar.evidence_basis: Major pearling port estimated at ~8,000 in Lorimer (1908), dipping during the 1930s-40s pearling depression before rising to 13,259 in the 1970 Qatar census.

Al-Baha-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Baha
Al-Baha-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Ghamid and Zahran highland market centre documented by Philby (1952), expanding modestly as a provincial administrative hub to ~12.8k by 1971.

Al-Majmaah-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Majmaah
Al-Majmaah-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Chief town of Sudayr oasis district described in Lorimer (1908) and Philby at ~4.2k, expanding with road links and regional administration to ~12.6k by 1971.

Al-Shihr-Yemen.name: Al-Shihr
Al-Shihr-Yemen.evidence_basis: Second port of the Qu'aiti Sultanate documented by Ingrams (1936) and NID (1946) at ~7k-9k, growing steadily via fishing and Indian Ocean trade to ~12.4k by 1971.

Nizwa-Oman.name: Nizwa
Nizwa-Oman.evidence_basis: Interior Imamate capital in Al-Jauf estimated at ~6,000 in Lorimer (1908), expanding through interior oasis trade and post-1955 unification to ~12k by 1971.

Salalah-Oman.name: Salalah
Salalah-Oman.evidence_basis: Dhofar administrative seat recorded at ~4,000 in Lorimer (1908), growing as Sultan Said bin Taimur's royal residence and British/Omani garrison during the Dhofar campaign to ~12k in 1971.

Layla-Saudi Arabia.name: Layla
Layla-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Capital of Al-Aflaj oasis district visited and estimated by Philby (1918) at ~3.5k-4k, expanding gradually as a southern Najd administrative town to ~11.6k by 1971.

Turaif-Saudi Arabia.name: Turaif
Turaif-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Founded in 1950 as a Tapline pumping station and border transit post near Jordan, growing through Aramco worker settlement and sedentarization to ~11.4k by 1971.

Zabid-Yemen.name: Zabid
Zabid-Yemen.evidence_basis: Historic Tihamah textile and scholarly city (~11k in 1900) that experienced interwar economic contraction (~8.8k per NID 1946) before stabilizing at ~11.2k by 1971.

Jidhafs-Bahrain.name: Jidhafs
Jidhafs-Bahrain.evidence_basis: Northern Bahrain agricultural village cluster west of Manama documented in Lorimer (1908) and Bahrain censuses, urbanizing to 11,152 in 1971.

Shaqra-Saudi Arabia.name: Shaqra
Shaqra-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Walled Washm district capital recorded in Lorimer (1908) and Philby (1922) at ~4k, growing gradually as a central Najd market town to ~10.8k by 1971.

Seeb-Oman.name: Seeb
Seeb-Oman.evidence_basis: Eastern Batinah town and site of the 1920 Treaty of Seeb (Lorimer 1908 ~4.5k), expanding in the late 1960s near Muscat to ~10.8k by 1971.

Riffa-Bahrain.name: Riffa
Riffa-Bahrain.evidence_basis: East and West Riffa inland seat documented in Lorimer (1908) at ~2.6k, rising in Bahrain official censuses to 6,623 (1959), 9,403 (1965), and 10,731 (1971).

Zinjibar-Yemen.name: Zinjibar
Zinjibar-Yemen.evidence_basis: Fadli Sultanate coastal town that expanded rapidly after the British-sponsored Abyan cotton irrigation scheme (1940s-50s) and post-1967 Governorate III capital status to ~10.5k by 1971.

Al-Qunfudhah-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Qunfudhah
Al-Qunfudhah-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Tihamah Red Sea port and Ottoman Asir supply harbour estimated at ~3.5k-4k in Arab Bureau (1916) and NID (1946), expanding gradually to ~10.4k by 1971.

Dumat al-Jandal-Saudi Arabia.name: Dumat al-Jandal
Dumat al-Jandal-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Historic Al-Jawf citadel and date oasis documented by Musil (1909) and Wallin/Lorimer at ~3.5k-3.9k, growing steadily to ~10.2k by 1971.

Ibri-Oman.name: Ibri
Ibri-Oman.evidence_basis: Chief oasis and caravan crossroad of Al-Zahirah described by Lorimer (1908) at ~5,000 souls, rising to ~9.8k by 1971.

Radaa-Yemen.name: Radaa
Radaa-Yemen.evidence_basis: Historic eastern plateau citadel and former provincial seat (NID 1946; 1975 YAR administrative divisions), expanding gradually from ~4.8k in 1900 to ~9.2k by 1971.

Barka-Oman.name: Barka
Barka-Oman.evidence_basis: Al-Batinah coastal fort and fishing-agricultural market documented by Lorimer (1908) at ~5,000 souls, reaching ~9.2k by 1971.

Rabigh-Saudi Arabia.name: Rabigh
Rabigh-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Pilgrim-route coastal town and palm oasis between Jeddah and Medina documented in Arab Bureau (1916) and NID Western Arabia (1946), growing from ~2.5k in 1900 to ~8.9k in 1971.

Al-Ula-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Ula
Al-Ula-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Walled northern Hejaz date oasis and Hejaz Railway station recorded by Jaussen & Savignac (1909) and NID (1946) at ~3.2k-3.8k, rising to ~8.6k by 1971.

Ibra-Oman.name: Ibra
Ibra-Oman.evidence_basis: Principal Al-Sharqiyah oasis and Zanzibar-linked merchant town recorded by Lorimer (1908) at ~4.5k, growing to ~8.4k by 1971.

Buraimi-Oman.name: Buraimi
Buraimi-Oman.evidence_basis: Omani sector of the contested Buraimi oasis cluster (Lorimer 1908; 1952-55 Buraimi dispute surveys), rising from ~4.2k in 1908 to ~8.2k by 1971.

Yarim-Yemen.name: Yarim
Yarim-Yemen.evidence_basis: High-altitude market town on the Sanaa-Taiz caravan road documented in NID (1946), growing from ~4.2k in 1900 to ~7.9k by 1971.

Sitra-Bahrain.name: Sitra
Sitra-Bahrain.evidence_basis: Eastern Bahrain island villages and BAPCO refinery terminal area documented in Lorimer (1908) and 1941-71 Bahrain censuses, reaching ~7.9k in 1971.

Sada-Yemen.name: Sada
Sada-Yemen.evidence_basis: Walled northern Zaydi Imamate stronghold and caravan market (NID 1946; 1975 YAR provincial census), rising modestly from ~4.2k in 1900 to ~7.8k by 1971.

Shibam-Yemen.name: Shibam
Shibam-Yemen.evidence_basis: Densely packed mud-brick tower-house city (~500 multi-storey houses within compact wadi walls per Ingrams 1936 and NID 1946), constrained by site area to ~5.5k-7.6k across 1900-71.

Rustaq-Oman.name: Rustaq
Rustaq-Oman.evidence_basis: Western Hajar fortress oasis documented by Lorimer (1908) and Wilkinson (1977) with extensive aflaj agriculture, expanding from ~3.8k in 1908 to ~7.6k by 1971.

Isa Town-Bahrain.name: Isa Town
Isa Town-Bahrain.evidence_basis: Planned model public-housing town inaugurated in November 1968 (absent from 1941-65 censuses), recording 7,501 inhabitants in the April 1971 Bahrain census.

Hajjah-Yemen.name: Hajjah
Hajjah-Yemen.evidence_basis: Imamic mountain fortress and provincial capital (NID 1946; 1975 YAR census provincial seat), expanding gradually from ~3.8k in 1900 to ~7.5k by 1971.

Amran-Yemen.name: Amran
Amran-Yemen.evidence_basis: Walled Hashid tribal basin town northwest of Sanaa documented in NID (1946) and 1975 YAR survey, growing from ~3.4k in 1900 to ~7.4k by 1971.

As-Suwayq-Oman.name: As-Suwayq
As-Suwayq-Oman.evidence_basis: Al-Batinah coastal palm-grove town documented by Lorimer (1908) at ~3.6k, expanding steadily with agricultural and coastal trade to ~7.4k by 1971.

Bahla-Oman.name: Bahla
Bahla-Oman.evidence_basis: Walled interior oasis and pottery hub near Nizwa recorded in Lorimer (1908) at ~3.5k, expanding gradually to ~7.1k by 1971.

Al-Wajh-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Wajh
Al-Wajh-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Northern Hejaz Red Sea port (~2.8k per Arab Bureau 1916; briefly swelled as 1917-18 Arab Revolt base before easing) growing to ~6.8k by 1971.

Al-Bayda-Yemen.name: Al-Bayda
Al-Bayda-Yemen.evidence_basis: Southeastern borderland town between Mutawakkilite Yemen and the Aden Protectorate (NID 1946), growing from ~3.1k in 1900 to ~6.4k by 1971.

Mesaieed-Qatar.name: Mesaieed
Mesaieed-Qatar.evidence_basis: Founded in 1949 as Qatar's deep-water crude oil export terminal (Umm Said), recording exactly 6,094 inhabitants in the 1970 Qatar national census.

Hidd-Bahrain.name: Hidd
Hidd-Bahrain.evidence_basis: Pearling town on southeastern Muharraq Island noted by Lorimer (1908), recorded in Bahrain censuses at 4,440 (1959), 5,230 (1965), and 5,269 (1971).

Ajman-United Arab Emirates.name: Ajman
Ajman-United Arab Emirates.evidence_basis: Small Trucial coastal sheikhdom (~1.5k in Lorimer 1908) recording 3,725 town residents (4,246 emirate total) in the 1968 Trucial States census.

Dukhan-Qatar.name: Dukhan
Dukhan-Qatar.evidence_basis: Founded in 1940 following the December 1939 Dukhan oilfield discovery by Petroleum Development (Qatar), expanding as an onshore oilfield company town to ~4.1k by 1970.

Umm al-Quwain-United Arab Emirates.name: Umm al-Quwain
Umm al-Quwain-United Arab Emirates.evidence_basis: Active pearling port in Lorimer (1908) (~4.2k) that declined sharply after the 1930s pearling collapse, recording 2,928 town residents (3,744 emirate total) in the 1968 Trucial States census.

Khor Fakkan-United Arab Emirates.name: Khor Fakkan
Khor Fakkan-United Arab Emirates.evidence_basis: Gulf of Oman natural harbour (Sharjah dependency) documented in Lorimer (1908) at ~1.4k and the 1968 Trucial States census at ~3.45k.

Khasab-Oman.name: Khasab
Khasab-Oman.evidence_basis: Musandam Peninsula coastal settlement of the Shihuh recorded by Lorimer (1908) at ~1.5k, expanding modestly to ~3.4k by 1971.

Al-Khor-Qatar.name: Al-Khor
Al-Khor-Qatar.evidence_basis: Northern Qatari pearling and fishing town documented in Lorimer (1908) at ~2.2k, easing in the 1930s-40s and recovering to ~3.1k in the 1970 Qatar census.

Mirbat-Oman.name: Mirbat
Mirbat-Oman.evidence_basis: Dhofar coastal frankincense and fishing port recorded by Lorimer (1908) at ~1.2k, growing gradually to ~2.55k by 1971.

Mocha-Yemen.name: Mocha
Mocha-Yemen.evidence_basis: Former coffee entrepot reduced by silting and Aden/Hudaydah competition to ~2.5k in 1900 and ~1.2k by NID (1946), recovering slightly after 1950s jetty repairs to ~1.9k in 1971.
